eras.name: Hand-crafted
eras.background: Engineers designed descriptors of edges, gradients and keypoints by hand, and learning was limited to a classifier on top. The approach was robust within limits but plateaued on hard recognition tasks.

eras.name: Deep CNNs
eras.background: Convolutional networks trained on large labeled datasets learned their own features and swept the recognition benchmarks. Detection split into accurate two-stage designs and fast single-pass ones.

eras.name: Transformers and diffusion
eras.background: Transformers spread from language to vision, and pretraining moved from fixed labels to image-text pairs. At the same time diffusion made high-quality image generation practical, and neural fields reshaped 3D.

eras.name: Foundation models
eras.text: One model, prompted for any image
eras.background: Large pretrained models began to handle open-ended tasks from a prompt: a point or box for segmentation, a question for a vision-language model. 3D moved to representations that render in real time.

nodes.label: SIFT
nodes.problem: Matching objects failed when scale, viewpoint or lighting changed.
nodes.idea: Detect keypoints and describe them with gradient histograms that stay stable.
nodes.impact: The workhorse of recognition and 3D reconstruction until CNNs.

nodes.label: AlexNet
nodes.idea: Learn the features end to end with a large CNN trained on GPUs.
nodes.impact: Learned features replaced hand-crafted ones across vision.

from.why: Hand-designed features like SIFT capped recognition accuracy.

nodes.label: Faster R-CNN
nodes.idea: A region proposal network shares the detector's CNN features.
nodes.impact: The accuracy baseline for detection, extended to segmentation by Mask R-CNN.

from.why: CNN features made detection accurate, but region proposals stayed slow and separate.

nodes.label: YOLO
nodes.idea: Predict every box and class in one pass over the image.
nodes.impact: The YOLO line became the default for real-time detection.

from.why: Two-stage detectors were too slow for real time.

nodes.label: NeRF
nodes.problem: Rendering a real scene from new viewpoints needed an explicit 3D model.
nodes.idea: Fit a network from position and direction to color and density, then volume-render it.
nodes.impact: Photoreal new views from photos alone, starting neural rendering.

nodes.label: ViT
nodes.idea: Cut the image into patches and feed them to a plain Transformer.
nodes.impact: Matched CNNs given enough data, so vision could share language's architecture.

from.why: Vision kept using CNNs while language had moved to Transformers.

nodes.label: DETR
nodes.idea: A Transformer predicts the set of objects directly.
nodes.impact: Showed detection could be end to end; later real-time detectors dropped NMS too.

from.why: Detectors still relied on hand-designed anchors and duplicate removal with NMS.

nodes.label: CLIP
nodes.idea: Train image and text encoders together on web image-caption pairs.
nodes.impact: Recognition from text prompts, and the encoder behind many later models.

from.why: Vision models, Transformers included, knew only the fixed classes they were labeled with.

nodes.label: Latent diffusion
nodes.problem: Diffusion in pixel space was too expensive for high-resolution images.
nodes.idea: Run diffusion in a compressed latent space, conditioned on text.
nodes.impact: Released openly as Stable Diffusion, putting text-to-image on consumer GPUs.

nodes.label: DiT
nodes.idea: Replace the U-Net with a Transformer over latent patches.
nodes.impact: Quality improves steadily with compute, and later image and video models build on it.

from.why: Its U-Net backbone was a different design from the Transformers scaling everywhere else.

nodes.label: SAM
nodes.idea: A promptable model trained on a vast mask dataset segments from points or boxes.
nodes.impact: Segments new images zero-shot and became a standard labeling tool.

from.why: Segmentation models were still trained per task and per dataset.

nodes.label: LLaVA
nodes.idea: Feed CLIP image features into an LLM and tune it on visual instructions.
nodes.impact: The template for open vision-language models.

from.why: Its image features already lined up with language, ready to feed into an LLM that could not see.

nodes.label: 3D Gaussians
nodes.idea: Represent the scene with 3D Gaussians and rasterize them.
nodes.impact: Real-time rendering of captured scenes, and it largely displaced NeRF in practice.

from.why: NeRF rendered too slowly for real-time use.

main.title: Stanford CS231n: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
main.why: Detection and segmentation, video, self-supervised learning, generative models, 3D and vision-language. In English.

main.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
main.why: ViT drops convolutions and runs a plain Transformer on image patches, which rivals CNNs when pretrained on enough data.

main.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
main.why: Labeled datasets limit what vision models learn, so CLIP trains on web image-caption pairs and classifies zero-shot from text prompts.

further.title: SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features

main.title: DINOv3
main.why: Labels limit how far vision encoders scale, so DINOv3 trains self-supervised and uses Gram anchoring to keep dense features clean.

main.title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
main.why: Region proposals were the bottleneck of detection, so Faster R-CNN adds a region proposal network that shares the detector's features.

main.title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
main.why: Two-stage detectors were too slow for real time, so YOLO predicts all boxes and classes in a single pass.

main.title: End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers
main.why: Detectors relied on hand-designed anchors and non-maximum suppression, so DETR predicts the set of objects directly with a Transformer.

main.title: Ultralytics YOLO26: Unified Real-Time End-to-End Vision Models
main.why: NMS adds latency to real-time detection, so YOLO26 removes it and handles detection, segmentation and pose in one pipeline.

main.title: Segment Anything
main.why: Segmentation models were trained per task, so SAM is a promptable model trained on a huge mask dataset that segments new images zero-shot.

main.title: SAM 3: Segment Anything with Concepts
main.why: SAM segments one object per prompt, so SAM 3 finds, segments and tracks every object matching a noun phrase or example image.

main.title: Visual Instruction Tuning
main.why: LLMs could not see images, so LLaVA feeds CLIP image features through a linear layer into an LLM tuned on GPT-4-written instructions.

main.title: Qwen3-VL Technical Report
main.why: For long documents and video, Qwen3-VL feeds a SigLIP 2 encoder's features through an MLP into Qwen3 LLMs with long context.

main.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
main.why: Pixel-space diffusion is expensive, so latent diffusion, the basis of Stable Diffusion, runs in an autoencoder's latent space with cross-attention for text.

main.title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers
main.why: DiT shows diffusion does not need a U-Net, and its Transformer backbone keeps improving as compute grows.

main.title: Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
main.why: Stable Diffusion 3 trains with rectified flow for straighter sampling paths and uses MM-DiT, a Transformer with separate text and image weights.

main.title: Wan: Open and Advanced Large-Scale Video Generative Models
main.why: Wan brings the diffusion transformer to video with its own video VAE, released as open models for text-to-video, image-to-video and editing.

main.title: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis
main.why: To render a scene from new viewpoints, NeRF fits an MLP from 3D position and view direction to color and density and volume-renders it.

main.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering
main.why: NeRF renders slowly, so 3D Gaussian Splatting optimizes a set of 3D Gaussians and rasterizes them in real time.

main.title: VGGT: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
main.why: 3D reconstruction usually needs slow optimization, so VGGT predicts cameras, depth and point maps from many views in one forward pass.
Off-the-shelf CLIP and BLIP failed on short product queries, so embeddings tuned on the catalog now rank ads.
Transcribing menu photos by hand was costly and slow, so DoorDash uses OCR plus an LLM, with a guardrail model that sends doubtful results to people.
